title: Co-projection for a closed immersion
statement:
In the finite-coefficient purity setting [def-pur-conventions], put $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow W$ be a closed immersion of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Work on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $K\in D^b_c(W,\Lambda)$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] and let $L$ be tensor-invertible in $D^b_{ctf}(W,\Lambda)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]: there is $M\in D^b_{ctf}(W,\Lambda)$ with $L\otimes^L M\cong\Lambda_W$ (and hence $M\otimes^L L\cong\Lambda_W$ by symmetry), as in [pur9-cs-def-invertible]. Use the derived operations [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and the constructible exceptional inverse image [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Then the canonical co-projection is an isomorphism
$$
 Ri^!(K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_W}L)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
 Ri^!K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_Z}Li^*L.
$$
Here the canonical map is the comparison of the right adjoints induced by the projection isomorphism $Ri_!(-)\otimes^L M\cong Ri_!(-\otimes^L Li^*M)$, whose underlying projection transformation is [def-exchange-projection].
No unrestricted ambient pro-etale exceptional adjunction is asserted.

proof.text: Write $P=Li^*$, $F=Ri_!$, $G=Ri^!$, and write $\otimes$ for the finite derived tensor. Choose the inverse $M$ in the statement. By [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude], $PL,PM$ lie in $D^b_{ctf}(Z,\Lambda)$. By the tensor and unit compatibility of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso], the images of $M\otimes L\cong\Lambda_W$ and $L\otimes M\cong\Lambda_W$ give $PM\otimes PL\cong\Lambda_Z$ and $PL\otimes PM\cong\Lambda_Z$. By [lem-sf-tensor-ctf], tensoring a bounded constructible complex by any of $L,M,PL,PM$ stays bounded constructible. Thus all the tensor functors used below have the stated constructible domains.

source.place: Hom calculation and final Yoneda paragraph; expanded categorical argument

proof.text: The total tensor and its derived descent have the closed symmetric monoidal structure of [lem-coef-sheaf-flat-model], with the ordinary sheaf derived tensor used here. The associator and the two inverse isomorphisms give natural isomorphisms $(B\otimes M)\otimes L\cong B$ and $(B\otimes L)\otimes M\cong B$. Thus $T_M=(-\otimes M)$ and $T_L=(-\otimes L)$ are quasi-inverse functors; the same holds for $T_{PM},T_{PL}$ on $Z$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-inverse-adjoint] on $W$ to choose an adjointification; use on $Z$ its pullback under $P$. Concretely the unit and counit on $Z$ are obtained by applying $P$ to those on $W$ and inserting its tensor and unit comparisons; their triangle equations are the images of those on $W$, since those comparisons respect composition and associativity as in [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]. This consistent choice gives natural Hom bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(B,C\otimes L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(B\otimes M,C)$ and their counterparts on $Z$. This cites an adjoint-equivalence theorem, rather than assuming an arbitrary pair of evaluation isomorphisms already satisfies the triangle identities.

source.place: Hom calculation and final Yoneda paragraph; expanded categorical argument

proof.text:
Use the constructible exceptional functor of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. The adjunction $F\dashv G$ is the bounded constructible restriction of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class]: every bounded constructible input has etale origin, as explicitly included in that theorem. A finite-dimensional compactification required there exists by [thm-nagata-compactification] and [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]. We use only this restriction, not an adjunction on all pro-etale complexes. For a constructible pro-etale sheaf, choose its constructible etale representative by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]. On the etale site, [sbc-thm-finiteness-finite-type] gives its bounded constructible compact-support image. The comparison [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison] identifies the exact pro-etale realization of this image with $F$ of the original sheaf, and [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] shows it is bounded constructible. Next use [lem-compact-support-direct-image-triangulated] to apply $F$ to the finite sequence of truncation triangles for any bounded constructible complex. Each triangle adds one shifted bounded constructible sheaf image, and a finite union of their cohomological intervals is bounded. Thus $F$ really is a functor between the bounded constructible categories used in steps 3 and 5. For any $A\in D^b_c(Z,\Lambda)$ and $K\in D^b_c(W,\Lambda)$, apply the genuine projection-formula theorem [fix-prop-projection-formula] at the finite-Tor object $M$. Together with step 2 and the two exceptional adjunctions it gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}_Z(A,G(K\otimes L))
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_W(FA,K\otimes L)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_W(FA\otimes M,K)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_W(F(A\otimes PM),K)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Z(A\otimes PM,GK)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Z(A,GK\otimes PL).
\end{aligned}
$$
All bijections are natural in $A$ and $K$. The projection theorem is applied with $A$ bounded constructible and $M$ finite-Tor; it is not inferred from the definition of the projection map.

proof.text: Fix $K$ and put $X=G(K\otimes L)$ and $Y=GK\otimes PL$. Both are objects of $D^b_c(Z,\Lambda)$, by the constructible typing in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] and step 1. By [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful], the natural bijections in step 3 are postcomposition with a unique map $c_K:X\to Y$. Apply the same statement to the inverse bijections to get $d_K:Y\to X$. Their composites induce the identity transformations of both representable Hom functors; injectivity of Yoneda gives $d_Kc_K=1_X$ and $c_Kd_K=1_Y$. Therefore $c_K$ is invertible. Naturality in $K$ follows by applying the same injectivity to the naturality squares of the Hom bijections.

source.place: Hom calculation and final Yoneda paragraph; expanded categorical argument

proof.text: Identify the canonical map rather than just an unspecified isomorphism. Put $H_1(A)=FA\otimes M$ and $H_2(A)=F(A\otimes PM)$. Step 3 supplies adjunctions $H_1\dashv(K\mapsto G(K\otimes L))$ and $H_2\dashv(K\mapsto GK\otimes PL)$. The natural projection isomorphism $H_1\xrightarrow{\sim}H_2$ is precisely the finite composite defined in [def-exchange-projection], whose invertibility was supplied by the theorem in step 3. Transport the second Hom bijection across that isomorphism, so that both right functors are now right adjoint to $H_1$. By [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint], the counit-compatible comparison between those right adjoints is unique. Its component at $K$ induces exactly the composite of the five Hom bijections of step 3, hence equals $c_K$ by the uniqueness in step 4. This is the canonical co-projection specified in the statement, and it is an isomorphism by step 4. The direction printed in the blueprint is the right-adjoint comparison for the inverse projection identification, so the comparison in the opposite direction is its inverse.

split_report.summary: Expanded the five natural Hom bijections, restricted them to the constructible domain, cited the actual projection theorem, proved representability gives inverse morphisms, and identified the canonical co-projection as the unique counit-compatible right-adjoint comparison. No new nodes. Recorded the implicit-domain correction and etale/pro-etale mismatch of the source Lean in the report.
split_report.blueprint: Steps 1-2 supply the inverse tensor and restriction used by the unit; step 3 is its five-line Hom calculation; steps 4-5 expand its final naturality, canonical-map and Yoneda sentence. The core lemma does not claim the unit’s separate twist and diagonal consequences.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q44-3e9e32ffb (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item's statement and all five proof steps in full, against the main-20261015 blueprint node and proof, the unit sk-lem-coprojection (_section and proof), and the full statements of every stmt/proof dependency. Statement: K in D^b_c contains the unit's D^b_ctf, so the item generalizes the unit. L is invertible in D^b_ctf with a ctf inverse M, which matches the unit (an inverse in D is RHom(L,Λ), which is ctf anyway). Coefficients are A_{E,n} on pro-étale sites, as def-pur-conventions prescribes. The 'separated schemes' hypothesis is the chapter convention and the only citer (lem-pur-immersion-twist) satisfies it. Small cases checked: i=id, Z empty, K=0, L=Λ[r], L=Λ(m)[2m]. Step 1: lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude, lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso and lem-sf-tensor-ctf(i) give the inverse PM and keep every tensor in D^b_c. Step 2: lem-coef-sheaf-flat-model gives the ambient monoidal structure and lem-weil-pbc-quasi-inverse-adjoint gives the tensor adjunctions. Step 3: thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class(2) applies, since G=ν^*f^×Rν_* is def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image and the inputs are D^b_c of étale origin, by lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin. FA is in D^b_c by the cited finiteness, comparison and triangle nodes. fix-prop-projection-formula applies with (A in D^b_c(Z), M in D^b_ctf(W)), and the PF direction matches def-exchange-projection. All five Hom bijections match the unit's display. Step 4: Yoneda in D^b_c(Z), with the typing taken from def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image. Step 5: det-sp-unique-right-adjoint identifies the canonical map in the stated direction. The route is the unit's. The tool_uses are accepted as black boxes. No new nodes; no cycle (checked over the full closure); no duplicate found by grep for co-projection, invertible and i^!. No SGA.
